clue.text: I call round, following in the meantime

indicators.note: following says the part built before it comes after the word 'in' in the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: round says the letters for 'call' go around the letter I

parts.note: to call something is to name or term it

explanation.surface: Someone describes making a phone call while waiting for something else to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I call round' reads as making a phone call; 'round' puts the call word around I, and 'following' sets that after the word 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim is a temporary period between two events, the meantime.

clue.text: Ant biting sheep's tail? Get vet

indicators.note: something biting has its teeth around another thing, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an ant is an example of an insect

indicators.note: the tail of the word sheep is its last letter

explanation.surface: A farmer sees an ant nipping a sheep's tail and decides to call the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' puts P, the last letter of 'sheep', inside INSECT; 'Get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine or check it carefully, as an inspector does.

clue.text: Animal having its rear licked

indicators.note: licked in the sense of thrashed or beaten, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A creature that has had its backside licked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licked' looks literal but means beaten: rearrange ITS REAR. The tarsier is a small big-eyed primate of South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsier is a small nocturnal primate, an animal of the Philippines and Indonesia.

clue.text: One who steps up to go over

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a pacer is a person or horse that steps at a measured pace

explanation.surface: Someone climbing steps in order to cross over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PACER around in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or run over points again, to go over them.

clue.text: Plant kiss here?

parts.note: a plant under which people traditionally kiss at Christmas, so 'Plant kiss here' reads both as an instruction and as a description

explanation.surface: An invitation to plant a kiss in a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb (plant a kiss) but is the noun: a Christmas plant under which couples kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Hung at Christmas, this parasitic evergreen is the plant beneath which people traditionally kiss.

clue.text: Stroke to leg when playing this?

definitions.text: Stroke to leg when playing this?

parts.words: Stroke to leg when playing this?
parts.note: reads like a cricket shot to the leg side, but describes a flirting game of touching legs under a table

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a batsman's shot played to the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'stroke to leg' is a shot to the leg side of the field; here the stroke is a caress of someone's leg in the flirting game.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing this flirtatious game means secretly touching a partner's legs or feet with your own, often under a table.

clue.text: Originally found old chemist using strong concentrate

indicators.note: originally means taking each word at its origin, its opening letter

explanation.surface: An old pharmacist discovered how to make a strong concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' applies to the five words after it: their first letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate is to direct attention closely, to fix one's mind on one thing.

clue.text: Seeking to profit from methane? OK, not exactly

indicators.note: not exactly says the letters are not given in their exact order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to make money from methane is told it is fine, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not exactly' rearranges METHANE and OK together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out for gain or advantage, especially for personal profit, is said to be on the make.

clue.text: Skater's leap from ice as loch was thawing

indicators.note: thawing ice changes its form, so the letters are melted into a new order

explanation.surface: A skater jumps off the ice of a Scottish lake just as it melts.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is LOCH plus WAS: 'thawing' rearranges LOCHWAS. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The salchow is a figure-skating jump taking off from the back inside edge and landing on the opposite foot.

clue.text: Rome rising to welcome person Monday such as this?

clue.text: Smartens up trees

definitions.meaning: to make neat and tidy, as in tidying one's appearance
conifers of the genus Picea, evergreen forest trees

explanation.definitionFit: Spruces up means makes smart; spruces are also a family of conifer trees, the Christmas-tree kind.

clue.text: Where Tom comes in worker's dress for Spooner?

indicators.note: Spooner's name signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a flat cap, the cloth cap traditionally worn by British working men
a flat cap, the cloth cap traditionally worn by British working men

explanation.surface: Some cat ends up dressed in workman's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat cap is the cloth cap of the traditional British working man; swap the FL and C sounds. Tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door lets a pet in and out, so it is how a tomcat enters the house.

clue.text: Requests for revelation near the Stations of the Cross?

definitions.text: Requests for revelation near the Stations of the Cross?

parts.words: Requests for revelation near the Stations of the Cross?
parts.note: religious imagery for asking voters, outside polling stations, to reveal where they put their cross on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: Pilgrims at the Stations of the Cross pray for a divine revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Stations' are polling stations and 'the Cross' is the X a voter marks on a ballot paper; 'revelation' is voters telling how they voted.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveys taken as voters leave polling places ask them to reveal how they cast their ballot.

clue.text: Number 20 of 24

indicators.note: 20 refers to the solution at 20 down, a word for rearranged letters, so this asks for a rearrangement

parts.note: 24 refers to the solution at 24 down, meaning at that point

explanation.surface: A list entry identified only by numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a thing that numbs, an anaesthetic, not a figure; '20 of' tells you to rearrange the letters of the answer at 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Once used as a general anaesthetic, this volatile liquid deadens feeling, so it is something that numbs.

clue.text: Number

clue.text: Imitating bird with one talon injured

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: an injured talon is damaged and bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bird with a damaged claw copies another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' tells you to rearrange 'one' (the Roman numeral) with the word talon, the bird coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulation is the act of copying or trying to equal another, so it means imitating as a noun.

clue.text: Old engagement ring judge involved with warrant

indicators.note: involved here means mixed up or entangled, so these letters are tangled together

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An old engagement ring becomes the subject of a legal case with a judge issuing a warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old engagement' looks like a former betrothal, but is an ancient battle. 'involved' rearranges O, J and WARRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary siege of Troy by the Greeks was an ancient conflict, engagement meaning battle.

clue.text: Need month to get better?

indicators.note: to get these letters the words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient is told they need a month to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange NEED MONTH; 'to get' signals the rearrangement and 'better' is the definition, recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness or injury is improving, getting better.

clue.text: Windy apartment you finally leased around third of June

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word you
around says the letters for 'leased' enclose another letter

parts.note: to lease a property is to let it

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of the word June

explanation.surface: An apartment you have finally rented has a draught by the third of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of 'you'; 'around' has the word for leased enclose the third letter of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent describes someone suffering from wind, gas in the gut.

clue.text: Type of gas left inside enemies quarters in the main

indicators.note: inside says the gas and the left letter go into the word for enemies

parts.note: foes are enemies
CS gas is a tear gas used in riot control

explanation.surface: A gas attack on enemy quarters at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'main' is the open sea; the answer is the contracted spelling of forecastles, crew's quarters in the bow of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship where sailors live, so these are crew quarters at sea.

clue.text: Judge grilled rarebit

indicators.note: a grilled dish is cooked and changed, so the letters of rarebit are reworked

explanation.surface: A judge cooks Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' and 'grilled' suggest a courtroom interrogation; 'grilled' rearranges RAREBIT, Welsh rarebit being cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes, a referee or adjudicator.

clue.text: Manuscript cut back before tests

indicators.note: before says the reversed piece goes in front of the abbreviation for manuscript
back says the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

explanation.surface: A manuscript was trimmed back before a set of tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manuscript cut back' looks like one idea, but 'back' turns only the word for cut, which goes 'before' the manuscript abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal tests of knowledge, as at school or university.

clue.text: In which one's relating integral to triangle?

definitions.text: In which one's relating integral to triangle?

parts.words: In which one's relating integral to triangle?
parts.note: sounds like a maths problem, but 'relating', 'integral' and 'triangle' are all made of the same letters, so the device links them

explanation.surface: A mathematician tries to connect an integral to a triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is calculus and geometry, but the three words 'relating', 'integral' and 'triangle' share the same eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This wordplay device rearranges the letters of one word or phrase to make another, as these three words show.

clue.text: Ring player who's left for west

indicators.note: L, the abbreviation for left, replaces W, the abbreviation for west

parts.note: a sweeper is a defensive football player behind the back line

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring who has moved from west to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' and 'player' suggest a boxer; the ring is an earring. A sweeper is a football defender; swap its W for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a small plain earring worn to keep a pierced ear from closing.

clue.text: One charmed by small firm's support

parts.note: Co, short for company, is a firm in a small form
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A small company's product that charms someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Snake charmers famously play to this snake, which sways from its basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake charmers in India traditionally perform with this hooded venomous snake.

clue.text: Dog trained in tea-garden

indicators.note: trained in the sense of shaped or disciplined into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog being trained in a tea-garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' suits a dog, but rearranges TEA-GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a very large breed of dog.

clue.text: Rummage around, but not game for a girl

indicators.note: around says the letters are turned around into a new order
but not says some letters are left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a game but finds a girl instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is rugby union; 'around' is the anagram sign and 'but not' removes those two letters from the rearranged pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Without taking sides, Ethel and Fred wed at that point

indicators.note: taking no sides means dropping each word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: Ethel and Fred stay neutral and get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without taking sides' strips the outer letters from Ethel and Fred, leaving THE and RE; 'and' and 'wed' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: There means in that place, at that point in time or space.

clue.text: An element of humility, for the most part unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of their order
for the most part takes most of the word, all but its final letter

explanation.surface: An uncommon touch of humility is found in most people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of humility, and 'unusual' rearranges HUMILIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithium is the lightest metal, chemical element number three.

clue.text: Tear in unsurveyed ropework

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the run of these clue words

explanation.surface: A rip appears in some rope work nobody inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as a rip; it is a teardrop, eye-drop. The letters sit in unsurvEYED ROPEwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-drop is a drop from the eye, a teardrop.

clue.text: Plant cultivated in good spray lacking pressure

indicators.note: cultivated in the sense of worked like soil, so the letters are turned over
lacking says a letter is taken out of the word spray

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A plant grown in a good spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes P from SPRAY, leaving SRAY; 'cultivated' rearranges IN, G and SRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is a shrub genus, the lilacs, also a name for mock orange.

clue.text: Idealist put diamonds on drill

indicators.note: on says the diamonds letter is placed against the drill word

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
a reamer is a tool for enlarging drilled holes

explanation.surface: An idealist puts diamonds on a drill.
explanation.walkthrough: D (diamonds, the card suit) goes with REAMER, a tool for enlarging holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone with unrealistic hopes, a visionary or idealist.
